questions.problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in meters, of a particle oscillating with periodically forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+7y=-\operatorname{sin}⁡pt,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Which value of the parameter $p$ causes the oscillator to resonate?
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of forced harmonic motion without damping is

$$
{y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=7\,⟹\,\omega =\sqrt{7}.
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{7}t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{7}t.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency $p$ of the external periodic force $f(t)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡pt$ coincides with the frequency of the complementary solution, which is $\omega =\sqrt{7}.$

Therefore, the oscillator experiences resonance when $p=\sqrt{7}.$

questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+ϕ)-\frac{3}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+ϕ)+3t\operatorname{sin}⁡t$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡t-3t\operatorname{cos}⁡t+t\operatorname{sin}⁡t$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $1.$ Therefore,
$\omega =1.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡t$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡t+D\operatorname{sin}⁡t).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =1$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[(2D-Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡t-(2C+Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)]+t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡t+D\operatorname{sin}⁡t) & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 2D\operatorname{cos}⁡t-2C\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & =3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=-\frac{3}{2}$ and $D=0.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=-\frac{3}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t.
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(t+ϕ)-\frac{3}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+ϕ)-\frac{3}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\frac{3}{2}t\operatorname{cos}⁡t$

Only solution I matches the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

questions.problem:
A particle of mass $0.5\,\text{kg}$ is attached to a massless spring. An external periodic force $F(t)=-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,\text{N}$ is applied to the particle.

The position of the particle is $y(t)$ (measured in meters), and $t>0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle moves with forced harmonic motion without damping and the system experiences resonance, what is the spring constant $k?$

$k=$
{{field-1}}${\text{kg/s}}^{2}$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of motion for a particle of mass $m$ moving with forced harmonic motion without damping under the action of a spring with spring constant $k$ and external force $F(t)$ is given by

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).
$$

Substituting our values for $m$ and $F(t)$ gives

$$
0.5{y}^{″}=-ky-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t).
$$

Simplifying and rearranging the above equation, we get

$$
{y}^{″}+2ky=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t).
$$

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ here represents simple harmonic motion, and it can be written as

$$
{y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t,
$$

where $A$ and $B$ are arbitrary constants of integration, and $\omega $ is the system's internal frequency.

In our case,

$$
{\omega }^{2}=2k\,⟹\,k=\frac{1}{2}{\omega }^{2}.
$$

The oscillator experiences resonance when the frequency of the external periodic force $f(t)=-4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t),$ which is $4,$ is equal to the frequency of the complementary solution $\omega .$

Therefore,

$$
k=\frac{1}{2}{\omega }^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {4}^{2}=8\,{\text{kg/s}}^{2}.
$$

$$
m{y}^{″}=-ky+F(t).

$$
0.5{y}^{″}=-ky+2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t).
$$

$$
{y}^{″}+2ky=4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t).

f(t)=4{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)=2(1+\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)),

questions.problem:
A particle is moving with forced harmonic motion without damping. The particle is acted on by an external periodic force
$f(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t).$
Assuming the system experiences resonance, which of the following could be used to represent the general solution for the position $y(t)?$

I. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{3}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

II. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{3}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

III. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+\frac{3}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

Note that $A,$ $B,$ $R,$ and $ϕ$ are constants.
questions.worked_solution:
Because the motion is undamped and the system experiences resonance, the forcing frequency equals the natural frequency $\omega .$

The external force is $f(t)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t),$ which is sinusoidal with frequency $4.$ Therefore,
$\omega =4.$

The complementary solution for the associated simple harmonic motion equation can be written in three different forms:

1\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)$

2\. ${y}_{c}=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(\omega t+ϕ)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)$

3\. ${y}_{c}=A\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t+B\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

At resonance, a sinusoidal trial at frequency $\omega $ duplicates the complementary solution, so we multiply by $t$ and take a resonant particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)).
$$

By substituting the particular solution and $\omega =4$ into the differential equation, ${y}^{″}+{\omega }^{2}y=f(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}[8(D-2Ct)\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-8(C+2Dt)\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)]+16t(C\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+D\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ 8D\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-8C\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) & =8\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}
$$

Equating coefficients, $C=\frac{3}{4}$ and $D=1.$ 

So, the particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=\frac{3}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t).
$$

Finally, then, the general solution is given by the sum of the complementary and particular solutions. So, it can be written in any of the following forms:

1\. $y=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{3}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

2\. $y=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t+ϕ)+\frac{3}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

3\. $y=A\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+B\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)+\frac{3}{4}t\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+t\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)$

Solutions I, II, and III match the forms above.
Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".
